cells.tense: You're in it, hands on the work, and it's holding.
cells.ask: Let one more pass in — the edge you've stopped trusting is the one worth checking. Not more hours, a finer eye — the work gets deeper, not narrower, and the finding is yours to keep.
cells.core:
You built it slow, and now it answers back. Standing at the bench with the whole shape in view, you can tell which join is true and which one you talked yourself into, and the knowing arrives without effort. That's the payoff of the repetitions nobody watched. Somebody asks how a piece comes together and you can show them from the inside out, because you've been inside it long enough to know.

What this is ready to feed is a closer look at what you've already got. Take something you finished and find the part you've been walking past on the way to the next thing. The eye you've earned can take the finer cut. Nothing needs to get bigger for the work to get deeper.
cells.sheetLine: You built this through showing up, and you can see what you built.
cells.verb: building something past the point where it stops being clever and starts being yours
cells.place: standing where what you've made finally shows you its whole shape

cells.tense: You're reaching for a finish line that keeps moving, and the reaching has more of you than the work does.
cells.ask: Go do something with people that has no outcome. The pattern doesn't need defending — it needs to be handed over. Sharing it is what holds it together, not grip.
cells.core:
Shown well, this is you teaching the method and shifting it as you go, watching someone else get it and finding the work gets truer in the telling. The pattern keeps your name on it and it belongs to whoever's following along.

Lately the pressure is doing the building and you're not in it. You're two steps past the current piece, checking whether the whole thing will hold years from now, and the checking has eaten the part where your hands are. More discipline won't loosen that. Get out of the workshop and into a room where people are glad you came. Bringing what you've made into company is what keeps it from going stiff.
cells.sheetLine: Gripping the work doesn't finish it, and it costs you everyone you'd share it with.
cells.verb: building something past the point where it stops being clever and starts being yours
cells.place: standing where what you've made finally shows you its whole shape

cells.tense: You put the tools down a while back and you've been standing beside the bench since.
cells.ask: Say plainly what you've built and that it's good. Naming it out loud is allowed — it's not bragging, it's putting the pattern where others can see it too, and that's the push that turns it outward.
cells.core:
There was a stretch where you looked at what you made and could say what was true about it. The seeing hasn't left. What left is the saying.

The bench is right there, and the first piece back doesn't have to be good — it has to exist and it has to be seen by someone who isn't you. Pick up the tools, finish something small, and put it where another person can look at it and tell you what they see. The building wants to move again through your hands, and the plain claim of what you've made is what lets it.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped building, and the pattern has nothing to stand on.
cells.verb: building something past the point where it stops being clever and starts being yours
cells.place: standing where what you've made finally shows you its whole shape

cells.tense: You're already deep in the work and calling it the routine doing its rounds.
cells.ask: Pick the piece you're most engaged with and tell one person your care for it is why you keep going. The drive has a source and it's yours to name.
cells.core:
You sharpen your eye at the thing you're making, day after day, and the noticing is happening whether or not anyone calls it yours. The work moves because you keep coming back to it, in how you check a line twice and know when to stop.

The steadier form of this is the schedule loosening and the direction coming from what you're actually drawn to, so the same hours feel pulled instead of carried. Check what you feel like doing before you check the calendar, and follow that for one afternoon. You'll find the momentum was never separate from you. Say that the next step is yours, and take it.
cells.sheetLine: The work is moving through you and you're letting it take the credit.
